a: if an XP profile is registered for production, it must satisfy the same embedded review and word-wrap/runtime capability matrix as every other family, and no existing evidence may be misreported as XP support.
m: RPG Maker XP is mentioned only as an example covered by the universal “no family-specific product capability gap” rule; the ledger does not separately specify an XP decoder or runtime implementation.

a: three independently implemented ports run the same conformance driver, and an unimplemented advertised operation fails conformance rather than returning an empty success.
m: Every runtime family implements a common port for loading, launch, stepping, input, tracing, choices, snapshots, capture, capability disclosure, and limitations.

a: a project for each of three families resolves its port and profile from registry data, while an unknown or omitted family produces a typed selection error.
m: Runtime families and profiles are selected from the same canonical registry vocabulary as decode rather than from family switches or fixture defaults.

a: adding a port crate without a conformance/matrix entry makes the gate fail before the family can be advertised.
m: Every production EnginePort implementation is discovered automatically or generated from one registry so it cannot escape parity testing.

a: a generated parity test detects any decoder without a corresponding declared runtime posture, any orphan runtime port, or any claim whose executable capability result disagrees.
m: Decode profiles, runtime ports, capability matrices, API schemas, and Studio rows agree on the family/profile and exact supported legs.

a: a minimal new port compiles and passes conformance using only facade imports, and a forbidden direct host-path or internal-state import fails the boundary check.
m: Engine ports depend on a stable substrate facade for assets, clock, input, state, output sinks, evidence, and managed artifacts rather than reaching through to host internals.

a: equivalent directory and packaged inputs produce the same asset reads, while traversal and an undeclared host-file read are denied and absent/decrypt-failed assets remain distinguishable.
m: Runtime assets are supplied through a read-only, hash-addressed virtual package with typed missing, encrypted, helper-gated, and unsupported outcomes.

a: two replays of one event log produce identical ordered state, trace, choice, and frame hashes, while changing one timestamp or input changes the expected checkpoint.
m: Input, clock, random, and external events are recorded and replayed deterministically.

a: each declared operation changes session state according to the contract, and every undeclared operation returns a typed capability error with no hidden state mutation.
m: Sessions expose start, pause, resume, step, jump, snapshot, restore, stop, and cancellation only when the selected port declares them.

a: snapshot, process restart, restore, and replay reach the same state/frame/trace hash; oversized, stale-version, wrong-profile, and corrupt snapshots fail explicitly.
m: Serializable runtime snapshots preserve enough port-owned state to resume deterministically within declared size classes and compatibility bounds.

a: a branching fixture enumerates the exact reachable options and targets, and an unsupported discovery request cannot return a fabricated empty branch list.
m: Ports expose typed branches, choices, targets, conditions, and reachability evidence rather than only a linear text trace.

a: a finite branching corpus reaches every expected moment once under its exploration policy, while a loop terminates with an explicit bounded-incomplete result.
m: A deterministic explorer can traverse declared route and choice space with bounded loop detection, state checkpoints, and coverage accounting.

a: selecting a stored moment in two sessions lands on the same source unit, state hash, and visible output, while a stale moment ID is rejected.
m: Stable scene, route, choice, line, and audiovisual moment identities support indexed jump or bounded replay-to-target.

a: changing only patched bytes changes the observed runtime text/frame, and deleting the patched artifact makes validation fail rather than fall back to source.
m: Runtime validation consumes the actual patched output package, not an unpatched source, bridge target string, or synthetic trace.

a: a composed scenario emits the expected cross-sink sequence, and dropping or reordering one required event fails the trace contract.
m: Text, choice, frame, audio, voice, state, syscall, warning, and approximation events use typed sinks with stable ordering and provenance.

a: an overlap fixture produces the oracle pixel hash and layer manifest, while swapping two layers or blend modes fails comparison.
m: Background, character, effect, UI, text, cursor, and choice layers compose with declared order, blend, transform, and clipping semantics.

a: clicks at recorded product coordinates select the intended engine target at three viewport scales, and the captured frame dimensions and transform metadata agree.
m: Ports can expose a framebuffer and translate product coordinates into engine input coordinates under scaling, letterboxing, and high-density displays.

a: the same long-target fixture produces checkable layout results for every registered family and a family-specific silent gap fails parity.
m: Every production family exposes the measurements needed for glyph, line, wrap, page, box, choice, and asset-fit QA or the framework disables that capability uniformly.

a: a known scene emits the expected ordered audio/voice events and associations, and a missing asset is reported rather than silently ignored.
m: Music, sound effects, voice, stop/fade/loop, and missing-asset behavior are represented with timing and source linkage even where actual playback is unavailable.

a: save, mutate, load restores the prior state and subsequent trace exactly; corrupt, stale, and wrong-profile saves fail with distinct typed diagnostics.
m: Save slots, serialization, load, rollback, and profile compatibility are port-owned deterministic operations.

a: every in-profile call in two real titles maps to a known implementation or declared approximation, and an unknown call stops or records an explicit limitation instead of defaulting.
m: Engine system calls are typed, allowlisted or emulated per profile, observable, and fail loudly when their semantics are unavailable.

a: deliberately unsupported graphics, syscall, and audio fixtures each produce a machine-readable limitation that survives API and UI rendering.
m: Partial VMs and renderers expose exact missing semantics, approximated operations, substituted assets, and fidelity limits.

a: one mutation in each category yields the exact failure class and no success evidence artifact is admitted.
m: Unknown opcodes, arguments, state shapes, assets, inputs, and renderer operations cannot be coerced into plausible successful output.

a: every report reference resolves from a fresh worktree, tampered bytes fail hash validation, and no report contains a checkout-local absolute path.
m: Captures, traces, snapshots, recordings, reference images, and reports are written through managed immutable references with hashes, retention, and privacy class.

a: omitting or mismatching any binding field makes the observation inadmissible for readiness or release.
m: Runtime observations bind project/profile, patched source revision, port/version, input log, state/trace/frame hashes, provenance, limitations, and privacy class.

a: a static-only fixture cannot satisfy a launched-observation query, and the UI displays the exact evidence class and limitations for every result.
m: Static decode, deterministic replay, partial-VM execution, launched-engine observation, reference capture, and human-confirmed evidence remain separate and never promote one another implicitly.

a: a comparison report names both producer classes and input revisions; swapping a replay frame in as a reference frame is rejected.
m: Native/browser/reference-runtime capture is explicitly distinguished from reimplementation output and can serve as a lawful comparison oracle.

a: a private run produces the complete declared capture set with verified hashes and no unintended redaction inside its controlled store.
m: Authorized local runs can retain complete frames, traces, and audiovisual evidence needed for debugging and comparison.

a: planted sensitive content and retail pixels are absent from the public bundle, yet its hashes and metrics remain linkable to the private evidence under authorization.
m: Public evidence is generated as a redacted derivative of private capture, excluding copyrighted frames/text, secrets, paths, and identifiers while retaining safe measurements and proof hashes.

a: timeline replay reproduces all checkpoint hashes and seeking to three recorded points yields the expected synchronized sinks.
m: A session can produce a deterministic timeline of input, text, choices, frames, audio, state checkpoints, and limitations for later replay and review.

a: deleting one required capture makes completeness fail with that moment named; zero captures cannot yield a passing report.
m: Capture plans state required moments, routes, screens, and artifact kinds and report observed, missing, failed, and out-of-scope items exactly.

a: the same portable replay fixture produces equivalent semantic traces on two execution targets, with declared renderer-only differences isolated in evidence.
m: Port and substrate contracts support browser/WASM, native desktop, and headless execution with platform-specific launch details held in profiles.

a: representative source and target scripts render and accept input on native and browser targets under a non-source-locale host with no mojibake.
m: Runtime text and product interaction use Unicode natively without requiring the source locale, fixed install path, or legacy system code page.

a: successful and unavailable launch cases on two transports serialize the same core contract, and command lines or local paths never enter public output.
m: Native executable, Wine/Proton, browser, NW.js, and engine-specific launcher transports share typed readiness, timeout, cancellation, process, and redacted-result semantics.

a: instrumentation observes every expected event in a known route while an uninstrumented baseline has identical game-state and frame outcomes.
m: Supported native or web engines can be instrumented at text, choice, route, screen, and lifecycle boundaries without changing product semantics.

a: two browser engines launch and capture through the same host page, and adding a third requires only a port plus registry entry.
m: Browser-capable engines expose launch URL, readiness signal, input bridge, capture hooks, and limitations as profile data rather than product conditionals.

a: differential execution touches every mapped in-profile item and fails the map if observed behavior or limitation differs.
m: Each family publishes which commands, syscalls, assets, input modes, render layers, and save features are implemented, approximated, or unsupported.

a: a deliberately hollow port can compile but fails conformance on missing state change, absent artifacts, or fabricated capability success.
m: The common runtime contract has positive, negative, cancellation, determinism, snapshot, artifact, and privacy tests that every claimed port must pass.

a: both titles reach declared checkpoints and emitted capability evidence through one profile-driven implementation; either failure blocks the family claim.
m: A family’s runtime claim requires the same port code to execute at least two real titles with no title-named mechanism.

a: live and recorded sessions drive the same player state model, and malformed or stale stream events are rejected rather than rendered.
m: The product player consumes runtime sessions, frames, choices, state, timelines, and errors through one typed streaming interface.

a: a running, completed, cancelled, unavailable, and failed session each produce distinct schema-valid status and correct UI treatment.
m: API and dashboard status disclose loaded profile, readiness, session phase, progress, active limitations, artifact links, and last typed failure.

a: a graph-based surface audit finds no exported runtime type, API, or UI route with zero production producer or zero product consumer.
m: Every retained runtime embedding, recorder, trace, branch, and state abstraction has an executable producer and consumer or is removed from the public contract.

a: two complete real archives execute their reachable command sets with zero unknown operations and match independently derived control-flow checkpoints.
m: The RealLive port interprets the complete in-profile bytecode and expression language, including state, control flow, functions, stores, memory, and entry semantics.

a: plaintext and encrypted scenes enter the VM with hashes matching decode output, and a decryption failure cannot be reclassified as an opcode error.
m: The runtime loads the same typed scene envelope, decompression, and second-level decryption stages used by decode.

a: a variable-behavior corpus reaches oracle values before and after snapshot restore, and out-of-range access fails explicitly.
m: Integer, string, local, global, stack, system, flag, and other declared variable classes obey engine-compatible indexing, width, lifetime, and snapshot semantics.

a: every choice modality selects each option under deterministic input and lands at the expected native target without index drift.
m: Jumps, calls, returns, conditionals, loops, selection variants, button areas, graphical choices, and interpolation drive exact branch and input behavior.

a: scripted interactions produce oracle text-window state and pixel comparisons across multiple window/markup cases.
m: Message windows, speaker/name presentation, pagination, wait/click state, backlog, ruby, interpolation, font/color, and clear/continue commands render with engine semantics.

a: a command corpus produces the expected state after each operation and a state-to-frame oracle detects any omitted mutation.
m: Object/layer creation, assets, position, transforms, visibility, opacity, clipping, transitions, effects, animation, and screen composition update a typed graphics state.

a: representative assets of every supported type match trusted decoded pixels and render into correct scene positions without synthetic placeholder substitution.
m: Supported G00 types decode into coherent surfaces and participate in layer composition at real dimensions.

a: checkpoints from two titles meet declared image-similarity thresholds against reference captures and contain the expected visible translated text.
m: Graphics, text, choices, effects, and cursor state produce visually meaningful frames rather than a text-only or blank canvas.

a: a scene with overlapping voice/music/effects yields the expected timing and lifecycle events, and unsupported decoding is disclosed.
m: NWA, OVK, voice, music, sound, fade, loop, and stop commands emit or play synchronized engine events.

a: all calls reached in two real titles are implemented or named as blocking limitations; no unrecognized call returns a fabricated zero.
m: Config-derived syscalls, area/input queries, mouse state, timers, window state, and platform effects have profiled semantics or exact limitations.

a: saving at a branch and restoring in a new session reproduces the next trace, choice, and frame hashes.
m: RealLive save/read formats, entry context, variable memory, scene position, and audiovisual state support deterministic resume.

a: the coverage receipt accounts for every reachable scene and known opcode in two real archives, with exact unreachable/out-of-scope sets.
m: Validation traverses all reachable scoped scenes/modules rather than proving only first text or one scene.

a: selected source and target observations bind the same unit IDs and frame locations, and reverting the patch removes the target observation.
m: Localized rebuilt archives launch or execute through the RealLive port and prove changed bytes in visible runtime output.

a: two real titles reach declared interactive checkpoints with zero unknown in-profile operations and nonblank rendered frames.
m: Siglus Scene/configuration state, expressions, flow, system functions, choices, text, graphics, audio, input, and saves execute through a real engine port rather than a compile-only scaffold.

a: one route yields aligned unit/choice checkpoints across all available modes, while a missing launched observation cannot be reported as captured.
m: Static trace, partial reimplementation, and launched-reference observations remain independently labelled and comparable.

a: representative checkpoints for two titles meet declared visual thresholds and every substituted or unsupported asset is disclosed.
m: Siglus image, character, text-window, choice, and transition assets compose into faithful frames.

a: two real titles spanning immediate and decoupled choices reach expected branches and frames with no build-ID conditional.
m: Softpal SCRIPT/TEXT state and Pal.dll calls execute through typed control, text, graphics, audio, input, and save semantics.

a: known checkpoints match reference structure and text placement, and an unimplemented display call makes fidelity evidence fail.
m: Softpal asset decoding, scene composition, dialogue/UI, choices, and Pal.dll display calls produce visually meaningful frames.

a: one MV and one MZ project expose all configured target units during automated playback and an omitted plugin hook appears as a coverage failure.
m: MV/MZ patched projects launch under browser/NW.js-compatible instrumentation that observes maps, events, dialogue, choices, UI, and plugin-profile text.

a: capability/evidence reports name the delegated runtime and a real project passes the same product contract without counting the launcher as decode proof.
m: Real Chromium/NW.js execution is an explicit faithful port model for browser engines rather than being mislabeled as native bytecode interpretation.

a: decoded choices from two projects emit the exact stored route IDs and an unresolved or foreign key fails rather than generating one ad hoc.
m: Choice and branch observations resolve to persisted project route-map identities instead of fixture-authored overlays.

a: two patched projects emit bound translated-text observations, while unavailable runtime dependencies return an explicit non-proof outcome.
m: VX Ace/RGSS3 projects can launch through a native-compatible or Wine transport with typed instrumentation and limitations.

a: equivalent packed and loose scenarios yield the same trace and visible output, including at least one encrypted real profile after lawful materialization.
m: Loose and XP3-backed KAG scripts share execution semantics for labels, macros, jumps, choices, message state, assets, and protected markup.

a: a scenario spanning the registered page-control tags emits the same ordered message boxes as a reference runtime and a coalescing mutation fails.
m: KAG message events respect actual page/click/clear boundaries rather than coalescing adjacent text runs.

a: two projects traverse configured routes with matching semantic observations across transports or record exact platform differences.
m: Ren’Py native and web transports expose labels, dialogue, menus, screen text, routes, callbacks, and screenshots through one profile.

a: two real projects replay declared routes and show patched text; an unsupported custom tag is surfaced rather than skipped.
m: TyranoScript browser instrumentation observes dialogue, choices, labels, jumps, variables, lifecycle, assets, and custom-tag limitations.

a: two protection variants observe patched units with stable structure links and no private path or key in artifacts.
m: Wolf profiles support the declared native or browser launch, common-event/database linkage, input, choices, and capture path.

a: growing and shrinking patched strings are observed at their expected runtime moments and every runtime unit links back to one native reference.
m: BGI decoded bytecode references, branches, text, and choice records can drive replay or launched observation bound to patched offsets.

a: two projects bind captured target text to I2 keys, while a non-I2 lookup is explicitly outside the profile.
m: A bounded Unity/I2 runtime profile observes table-key lookups and visible localized output without claiming arbitrary Unity behavior.

a: two Naninovel projects produce profile-specific runtime observations and no Unity/I2 adapter evidence can satisfy the claim.
m: Naninovel receives its own launch, instrumentation, route, and capture capability model.
